fixtures.question: Should the United States continue current immigration enforcement policy?

pro_theses.text: The United States should continue current immigration enforcement, including interior removals and border controls, to uphold the rule of law.
Maintaining present immigration enforcement policy is necessary to deter illegal entry and protect public safety.

con_theses.text: The United States should stop current immigration enforcement practices because they are cruel and inflict unnecessary harm on migrants and families.
Continuing today's immigration enforcement policy is unjust and should be rolled back in favor of more humane alternatives.

fixtures.question: Has Iran lost control of the Strait of Hormuz?

pro_theses.text: Iran has lost effective control of the Strait of Hormuz and can no longer unilaterally dictate transit there.
Evidence shows Iran no longer controls passage through the Strait of Hormuz as it once did.

con_theses.text: Iran has not lost control of the Strait of Hormuz and still retains decisive leverage over the waterway.
Claims that Iran lost control of the Strait of Hormuz are false; Tehran remains the dominant local power there.
